title: 2013 AMC 10A Problem 11
statement: A student council must select a two-person welcoming committee and a three-person planning committee from among its members. There are exactly \(10\) ways to select a two-person team for the welcoming committee. It is possible for students to serve on both committees. In how many different ways can a three-person planning committee be selected?

solutions.text:
Let \(x\) be the number of students. Then the number of ways to pick a two-person committee is \[ \binom{x}{2} = \dfrac{x(x - 1)}{2}. \] We know that this equals \(10,\) so \[ x^2 - x = 20 \]\[ x^2 - x - 20 = 0. \] Factoring yields \[ (x - 5)(x + 4) = 0 \]\[ x = 5, \] since there cannot be a negative number of students.

Then, the number of ways to pick a \(3\)-person committee is \[ \binom{5}{3} = \binom{5}{2} = 10. \]

Thus, A is the correct answer.
hints: Let \(n\) be the number of council members and use \(\binom n2=10\)
